newsitem.title: UK: Oxford University postpones business school.
newsitem.headline: Oxford University postpones business school.

text.p: Oxford, one of the world's oldest and most prestigious universities, said on Thursday it had postponed until June a decision on whether to build a controversial business school funded by a Syrian-born tycoon.
Oxford said it was not practicable to build the school on one of the university's many cricket grounds. Last November university dons (academics) voted against using the cricket ground.

Many outsiders saw the vote as a snub for Said, a friend of former conservative prime minister Margaret Thatcher. He has been accused of making part of his fortune through arms dealing -- a charge he strenuously denies.

A university statement on Thursday said: "The University of Oxford and Mr Wafic Said and his fellow Trustees of the Said Business School Foundation have jointly agreed that it is not practicable to proceed with the proposals to build new premises...for the University's Business School."
An alternative site had not been identified but Oxford had "agreed that the search should continue until the end of the Trinity Term" on June 21.

"A final decision will then be taken on whether it is possible to proceed. The university and the benefactor remain firmly committed to the goal of developing a world-class business school," the university said.
Since Said's offer of 20 million pounds ($34 million) to build a business school was accepted by the university in July, the whole project has been dogged by controversy.
Some professors doubt whether a business school fits into the academic ethos of the ancient university.
